data.summary: On 2026-10-13, urlquery scans show Microlink running custom browser code against api.usaspending.gov. The code POSTed Base64-encoded queries to the TAS quarterly-balances API and got FY2023 public data back.
data.description:
Three urlquery.net reports from 2026-10-13 (UTC) show the same Base64-obfuscated async function aimed at api.usaspending.gov:

14:46:41, report ac1276ce-239e-4caa-9ef7-aaf2b582c92a: the function was sent as a query parameter directly to api.usaspending.gov. The screenshot shows "Web Page Blocked!".
14:57:08, report 02d3343a-9131-4461-bfe4-371fb123af13: the same function went through api.microlink.io. The screenshot shows status "success", isFulfilled true and four fiscal-quarter records.
15:48:54, report 2b13a1fe-a885-49eb-bc26-973199f60b20: a second Microlink submission with the identical function. The screenshot shows the same four records.

What the code does: Microlink opens a browser on api.usaspending.gov. The function then uses page.evaluate to decode a path and a JSON body from Base64 and POSTs to /api/v1/tas/balances/quarters/total/. The decoded query asks for unobligated_balance_cpe, grouped by reporting fiscal year and quarter, for federal account ID 5599 and FY2023. The data is returned through Microlink's result.

Outcome: Both Microlink screenshots show status success, a fulfilled function, a pagination count of 4 (FY2023 Q1-Q4), and a current URL on the intended endpoint. The Microlink response metadata has the same SHA-256 (b7b7a50dcd3c26b752f952bb33e45126ecc6bd1c28e2b64e58ec019ff11f025c) in both reports. That means the captured content was identical. It does not prove two separate runs, because caching or replay can't be ruled out. The response body is marked unavailable, so the result rests on the screenshots.

Uncertainties: The direct request was not a normal POST, so the block does not prove a bot-protection bypass. It is still plausibly the first attempt before switching to Microlink. We don't know who ran this, which model was used, how many agents there were, or whether they coordinated. AI involvement is inferred: niche task parameters, code carried inside a scan URL, and third-party browser execution all match documented agent workflows. Human-written automation is still possible. The IP shown on the block page (195.64.118.152) belongs to the scanner, not the operator. The "Attack ID" on that page is a product diagnostic, not evidence of an attack.

Novelty: Earlier research already documents USAspending quarterly-balance queries (May 2026) and Microlink-style proxies. This is a new October instance, not a first discovery.
